## 1. Why this change A CUDA graph's batch size means different things for two kinds of step: - A prefill or mixed batch is sized by its **tokens**. - A uniform decode batch, where every request has the same query length `q = 1 + K`, is sized by its **requests** and `q`. On main, model runner V2 captures both from one token list (`cudagraph_capture_sizes`, capped at 1024 tokens on GB200). A decode graph must be a list entry divisible by `q`, so the larger K is, the fewer decode requests the graphs cover, and every mixed batch above 1024 tokens runs eagerly. Example: with the 1024-token cap and K = 7 (`q = 8`), decode graphs cover at most 128 requests. Uniform decode batches above 128 requests exceed main's FULL coverage. This is the "separate prefill/decode graph sizes" item of the Q4 roadmap (#61024). ## 2. What this PR changes This PR adds five configuration fields: a cap and a capture-size list for each kind of graph, plus a token budget for uniform decode graphs. Prefill coverage is configured in tokens; uniform decode coverage is configured in requests. | field | unit | controls | default on SM100 (GB200, B200) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens` | tokens | Maximum token count for prefill, mixed, and fallback decode PIECEWISE graphs | `min(8192, max_num_batched_tokens)` | | `prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes` | tokens | Token counts at which those graphs are captured | Default prefill grid up to the cap: 54 sizes at 8192 tokens | | `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests` | requests | Request-count cap for uniform decode FULL graphs, before applying the token budget | `max_num_seqs` | | `decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes` | requests | Request-count capture sizes, converted by each runner into `n × q` tokens | Default decode grid up to the cap: 64 sizes at 1024 requests, before applying the token budget | | `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens` | tokens | Maximum token count of each uniform decode graph | 8192 | For either kind, setting only a cap generates the default grid up to that cap. An explicit list selects the capture sizes; if a cap is also supplied, the list must fit within it. An empty list disables that kind. The decode request grid is the starting point for capture planning. Each runner uses its own query length `q` and captures only shapes that fit its execution limits and token budget. At the default 1024-request cap, the target captures 64 decode sizes through 1024 requests for K ≤ 7, or 48 sizes through 512 requests for K = 15. Wider target decode batches try the prefill token graphs before falling back to eager execution. The token budget also bounds adaptive-verification graphs. It does not bound one-token draft decodes, which reach `max_num_seqs` whatever the decode caps are (only `[]` turns them off). On other GPUs, the prefill and target decode defaults stay as on main. **How the defaults were chosen.** Defaults trade padding and coverage against memory/startup cost; current padding measurements are in appendix A. The decode budget limits wide graphs (why 8192: section 5.1); explicit lists/caps support workload- and parallelism-specific tuning. The default configuration and tuned performance ceiling are separate evaluation targets.
Grids, other GPUs and edge rules Defaults on other GPUs: the prefill cap is the platform's `max_cudagraph_capture_size` (512 on H100 / H200) and the prefill sizes are main's list; the decode cap is main's reach, 512 / (1 + K) requests, with main's request counts; there is no decode token budget. | what you set for a kind | graphs captured for that kind | | --- | --- | | nothing | the default grid up to the default cap | | a cap only | the default grid up to that cap | | a list only | exactly those sizes | | both | the list; a size above the cap is an error | | `[]` | none | - **Grids.** - **Prefill** / mixed (tokens): 1, 2, 4, every 8 up to 64, four sizes per doubling up to 1024 (…, 512, 640, 768, 896, 1024), then multiples of 256 through 7680, followed by 8192 — **54 capture sizes** at the default cap. Between 64 and 1024 tokens, a mixed batch pads by at most 25%, reducing padding-induced crossings of a model's own shape threshold (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's decoder-replay trim at 768 tokens; DEP section). - **Decode (requests):** every count from 1–6; then 8–16 in steps of 2, 20–48 in steps of 4, 56–128 in steps of 8, 144–352 in steps of 16, and 384–1024 in steps of 32. **64 capture sizes before applying the decode-token budget**; the default 8192-token budget keeps all of them for K ≤ 7 and limits target K=15 to **512 requests / 48 sizes**. - **Adaptive verification (tokens):** 1, 2, 4, 8; then four additional sizes per doubling through 1024—for example, 10, 12, 14, 16, followed by 20, 24, 28, 32. Above 1024, use steps of 128 through 4096, then steps of 256. The cap is `min(decode request cap × (K + 1), max_num_batched_tokens, max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens)`; **K=5 with a 1024-request cap gives 64 sizes through 6144 tokens**. Adaptive verification picks its verify width from the captured sizes, so this grid is finer than the prefill grid. - Sizes above `max_num_batched_tokens` (prefill) or `max_num_seqs` (decode) are dropped with a warning. `[]` for both kinds turns decoder CUDA graphs off. Under `cudagraph_mode` FULL or PIECEWISE (no separate decode routine) every batch uses the prefill sizes; under FULL_DECODE_ONLY the prefill sizes are not captured and do not count toward the recorded maximum. - Setting one kind leaves the other kind's graphs unchanged. Exception: DSpark, DFlash, DFlash2 and LiLiCorr are also capped by the resolved `max_cudagraph_capture_size` divided by their `q`. That value is the largest token count over the language-model/drafter graphs: prefill sizes, target decode `n · q`, one-token draft decodes and adaptive-verification sizes. At the SM100 defaults with K ≤ 7 it is the 8192-token prefill cap. Off SM100 with an EAGLE-family drafter it is the one-token draft decode reach (`max_num_seqs`, 1024), above the 512-token prefill cap. - `cudagraph_capture_sizes` and `max_cudagraph_capture_size` are deprecated on model runner V2. Set alone, they seed both kinds as on main, with a warning; combined with the new fields, they raise. Adaptive verification, DSpark and one-token draft decodes do not reproduce main's graphs under them. Model runner V1 is unchanged and rejects the new fields. ```bash # Before: one cap for both kinds, in tokens. --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 1024}' # After: delete it to take the defaults, or set each kind in its own unit. --compilation-config '{"max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens": 8192, "max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests": 256}' # Prefill instance of a disaggregated deployment: no decode graphs. Adaptive verification # needs decode graphs and is rejected with this; a prefill instance never verifies, so disable it there. --compilation-config '{"decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes": []}' # Decode instance of a disaggregated deployment: FULL decode (and adaptive verification) only, no PIECEWISE graphs. --compilation-config '{"prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes": []}' ```
## 3. Which graphs run ```mermaid flowchart TD C["Resolved config
prefill grid (tokens) · decode grid (requests) · decode budget (tokens)"] C --> T["Target
PIECEWISE: prefill / mixed, by tokens
FULL uniform decode: q = 1 + K, by requests, up to the decode budget
wider decodes: PIECEWISE, or eager without a prefill grid"] T -->|"adaptive verification on"| V["FULL varlen decode, by tokens
replaces the target's uniform decode graphs"] C --> E["EAGLE / EAGLE3 / single-module MTP"] E --> E0["Draft step 0: copies of the target's shapes
PIECEWISE + FULL at q = 1 + K"] E --> E1["Draft steps 1 … K − 1: FULL, q = 1
default request grid through max_num_seqs"] C --> B["DSpark (q = K) · DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr (q = K + 1)
FULL, one graph per draft round"] C --> M["Multi-module MTP (q = 1 + K, the target's layout)
after a decode step: 1 FULL graph with all K modules, by requests
after a prefill / mixed step: K PIECEWISE runs, by tokens"] ``` Each runner owns its graphs and picks among them by its own inputs. A decode step wider than the decode budget falls back to the PIECEWISE prefill graphs; on an instance with an empty prefill grid, such as a disaggregated decode instance, it runs eagerly. The list/cap labels above refer to the exact fields in section 2; a graph mode or attention backend can restrict which paths are available. **YOCO decoder replay: rule unchanged.** Its breakable PIECEWISE grid is still derived from `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, which now follows the prefill cap: 32 sizes up to 8192 tokens (main: 8 up to 1024; memory in section 5). Replays above the grid run eagerly. Forcing every replay eager (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DSpark K5 + AV, GSM8K twice per launch) kept GSM8K answer agreement with the graph runs at the graph-vs-graph level (TP4 / 256K 98.6–99.1% vs 99.0%, DEP4 / 64K 99.0–99.4% vs 99.2%); the debug switch had no counter, so it does not prove that every replay ran eagerly. [Implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cff6224872ad24b10c224bc4186778dcd90a1b21/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py#L26). **DEP applies these grids to per-rank execution batches.** Ranks synchronize execution mode and padding before the final dispatch; API concurrency is not a per-rank capture size. Dynamic SD is currently disabled for DP > 1; AV is a separate setting. [DP dispatch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cff6224872ad24b10c224bc4186778dcd90a1b21/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/dp_utils.py#L43). Every step picks the smallest captured graph that holds it; a step no graph holds runs eagerly. | step | graph | sizes from | decode budget | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | target prefill / mixed batch | PIECEWISE, by tokens | prefill grid | – | | target uniform decode | FULL at `q = 1 + K`, by requests | decode grid; wider decodes run PIECEWISE (eagerly with an empty prefill grid) | yes, up to budget / `q` requests | | target verification with adaptive verification (DSpark, DFlash) | FULL varlen: query lengths 1 … 1 + K in one batch, by tokens | adaptive-verification token grid | yes, up to the budget in tokens | | EAGLE, EAGLE3, single-module MTP: draft step 0 | the target's shape: a PIECEWISE copy for a mixed batch, a FULL copy at the target's `q = 1 + K` for a uniform decode (under dynamic SD, one `q = 1 + k` per tier) | the target's prefill and decode grids | yes, for the FULL copies | | same drafters, draft steps 1 … K − 1 | FULL at `q = 1`, by requests | default request grid through `max_num_seqs`; an empty decode list disables this path | no | | DSpark (`q = K`); DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr (`q = K + 1`) | FULL, one graph per draft round | decode grid, also capped at `max_cudagraph_capture_size` / `q` | yes, up to budget / `q` (all 1024 requests for DSpark K = 7) | | multi-module MTP: draft round after a uniform-decode target step | **one** FULL graph at the target's `q = 1 + K` holding all K module forwards and samplings | the target's decode grid (Inkling K=8: 61 graphs up to 910 requests; main 76 up to 112); wider decodes run as in the next row | yes | | multi-module MTP: draft round after a prefill / mixed target step | **K** breakable PIECEWISE runs, one per module (breakable models, e.g. Inkling, Step5, Kimi-K3); other models run the K modules eagerly | prefill grid (Inkling: 54 sizes up to 8192; main 91 up to 1024) | – | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash YOCO decoder replay | breakable PIECEWISE, by replay tokens (unchanged) | rule unchanged; bound now 8192 (32 sizes; main 8 up to 1024) | no | | n-gram, draft model | none (eager) | – | – | **The rule for `q`:** a FULL decode graph is captured at the query length its runner sees per request. The target and EAGLE-family draft step 0 see the 1 + K verified positions (`q = 1 + K`); later EAGLE-family steps add one token (`q = 1`); DSpark drafts K positions per round (`q = K`); DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr and multi-module MTP draft K + 1 (`q = K + 1`). Dynamic SD changes the target's verification length. EAGLE-family drafters also shorten their drafting sequence, while DSpark and DFlash currently retain their maximum draft-block width (K = 7: all 1024 requests under the 8192-token budget). A graph for `n` requests holds `n · q` tokens, which is what the decode budget bounds. **The decode budget** applies to every FULL uniform-decode graph with `q > 1`: the target's, the drafter copies of it, DSpark, DFlash and multi-module MTP. Each runner divides it by its own `q`: at K ≤ 7 the target and every drafter reach the 1024-request cap, while at K = 11 the target (`q = 12`) reaches 682 requests and DSpark (`q = 11`) 744. Why 8192: section 5.1. Adaptive verification's token-keyed graphs stop at the budget too. One-token draft decodes (`q = 1`, at most `max_num_seqs` tokens) are not bounded by it. **Graph count, one example:** MiniMax-M3 with EAGLE3 K = 3 at the GB200 defaults. | runner | this PR | main | | --- | --- | --- | | target PIECEWISE | 54, up to 8192 tokens | 83, up to 1024 tokens | | target FULL (`q = 4`) | 64, up to 1024 requests | 81, up to 256 requests | | drafter step 0 (copies of the target's) | 54 + 64 | 83 + 81 | | drafter steps 1–2 (`q = 1`) | 64, up to 1024 requests | 83, up to 1024 requests | | **total** | **300** | **411** | Current total memory is in section 5. Counts for every runner, K, dynamic SD tier and for GPUs other than SM100: appendix G (recomputed on the measured base; every launch's logged capture counts match).
Scope: vision encoder and TPU graph planning The new prefill/decode fields configure **GPU language-model and drafter graphs**. Vision-encoder graphs have an independent shape contract; TPU uses XLA compilation rather than CUDA graph replay. | Component | Size / execution contract | Controls | | --- | --- | --- | | GPU vision encoder | Visual **output tokens**, item/frame capacity, model paths and optional shape axes; captures a whole encoder path, including attention, with eager fallback | `cudagraph_mm_encoder`, `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch` | | GPU language-model prefill / decode | Scheduled tokens / requests × query length; PIECEWISE / FULL as described above | This PR's prefill/decode fields | | TPU language-model backbone | Token and request buckets select JAX/XLA executable shapes; these are not CUDA FULL/PW graphs | `MIN_TOKEN_BUCKET`, `VLLM_TPU_BUCKET_PADDING_GAP`, `additional_config.compilation_sizes`, `ATTN_BUCKETIZED_NUM_REQS` / `ATTN_CUSTOM_NUM_REQS_BUCKETS` | | TPU vision encoder, supported budget-manager path | Reuses GPU encoder budget generation and packing, with JIT compilation replacing CUDA capture/replay | Existing `cudagraph_mm_encoder` / `encoder_cudagraph_*` fields | **Vision defaults and counts.** Encoder capture is off by default. Its empty budget list means **automatic sizing**, unlike the new decoder lists where `[]` disables that kind. Budgets double from a model-provided minimum and include the maximum. For Qwen3-VL, with `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` and sufficient context, this gives `[64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192]`: **8 graphs**. Model paths and extra axes multiply the count: at the same cap, Gemma4 with five enabled row widths has **40**, and DeepSeek-OCR's global/local paths have **14**. These are source-derived examples, not measured captures in this PR. Multi-path models may regenerate their own per-path grids from the maximum; an explicit encoder list is not universally an exact per-path list. [Planner and count formula](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/vllm/v1/worker/encoder_cudagraph.py#L82-L280). Changing the decoder prefill cap alone does not resize encoder graphs. Encoder auto-sizing can depend on the scheduler token cap and model context. Encoder preparation and cached-output cloning remain outside graph replay. `compile_mm_encoder` is a separate compilation switch; `enforce_eager` disables encoder capture, whereas decoder mode `NONE` alone does not. **Memory / performance.** Encoder capture owns a separate shared graph pool plus persistent per-budget input/output buffers; runtime embedding caches and gather buffers add further costs. Graph count alone does not determine GiB. Upstream's GB200 Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B benchmark reports mean encoder latency **5.42 → 4.36 ms** with FLASHINFER and an explicit nine-size grid; that is an encoder benchmark, not an E2E result from this PR. See the [design and reproduction commands](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md). No encoder-specific memory measurement is claimed here. The pinned base already checks `runner.needs_cudagraph_capture()` before returning early for decoder mode `NONE`; the earlier encoder-only profiling caveat is resolved in the base ([current guard](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/08e3f264583e57199c167c577f3b445a58c155ab/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L944-L948)). Encoder-specific memory and runtime evaluation remain outside this refresh. **TPU scope.** At plugin `7840339bd3`, a DP1 configuration with an 8192-token cap and default minimum 16 has **10 token buckets**, doubling from 16 to 8192. This is not the total executable count: request buckets, embedding/PCP variants, SD and helper functions add variants. A positive padding-gap setting trades more compiled shapes for less padding. This PR's split CUDA-grid fields do not configure those TPU backbone buckets. The TPU vision manager already shares the encoder planner, but currently declines extra capture axes and assumes a single default path. [Token buckets](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/utils.py#L163-L263), [runner](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/tpu_runner.py#L1099-L1207), [vision JIT manager](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/mm_encoder_jit_manager.py). No TPU runtime or HBM validation is claimed. **Integration direction:** share shape planning, dispatch diagnostics and memory accounting while retaining explicit units and backend execution. A concrete planning follow-up is to prune infeasible budget/axis pairs: in the Gemma4 example above, 10 of 40 pairs have a budget below one image/frame row width and cannot be selected for nonempty replay. This is a source-derived pruning opportunity, not a measured memory saving ([shape contract](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py#L1710-L1900)). Keep encoder budget overrides; do not silently copy the decoder grid into vision or TPU. Per-path/axis budgets remain follow-ups; encoder-only profiling is already handled by the pinned base. This refresh does not add encoder changes.

### 5.2 DFlash graph memory and the MiMo limitation DFlash and DFlash2 drafters have no PIECEWISE fallback, so at K7–K8 the 8192-token budget gives their FULL graphs up to 8190 tokens (main: about 1024). On MiMo this adds 10.2 GiB of graph memory, from two sources. The target's widest prefill graph (8192 tokens) takes 5.4 GiB more than main's (1024 tokens), mostly FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE workspace. The DFlash drafter's widest graph (8190 tokens) takes 5.45 GiB, against 0.68 GiB on main, because it materializes full-vocabulary draft logits three times (the TP all-gather output, a contiguous copy and the vocabulary remap; about 2.07 GiB each). None of this is a leak. `graph_capture()` gives the target and the drafter separate capture streams, and the caching allocator keeps free graph-pool blocks per stream, so neither runner reuses the other's free blocks. Capturing every graph on one stream per device (#59537) brings MiMo from 14.16 to 12.84 GiB of graph memory; it also helps beyond DFlash: DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark K7 with AV 12.67 → 9.01 GiB, GLM-5.3 DFlash2 12.41 → 11.12 GiB, Qwen3-8B DFlash 5.75 → 4.77 GiB (main's MiMo: 3.93 → 3.76 GiB; one launch each, GSM8K unchanged). The order of capture then matters, because the graphs captured second reuse the free blocks of those captured first: capturing MiMo's drafter, its widest graphs, before the target brings MiMo to 9.89 GiB and lets the vLLM recipe command (`--max-model-len auto`, adaptive verification on) start at the full 1,048,576-token context, as on main, but costs 1.68 GiB on DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark and 0.26 GiB on GLM DFlash2, so it is not a default. With the shared stream alone, the recipe command still does not start: a 1,048,576-token request needs 15.06 GiB of KV cache and 13.96 GiB is left. **Known limitation:** with this PR, that recipe command (`--max-model-len auto`) fails at startup on 4x GB200. With the extensible KV cache, `auto` is fitted before CUDA graphs and warmup take their memory, and main only checks the fitted length afterwards. The error names the length that fits (`estimated maximum model length is ...`). An explicit `--max-model-len 524288` starts and passes GSM8K (93.8% / 94.5%). Lowering `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens` to 4096 cuts graph memory to 11.05 GiB. How the grids were chosen **Data.** The rule was derived from traces on earlier PR heads; the padding cost in (c) is a current measurement. **The rule.** Each grid captures a graph wherever padding to the next size would cost more than a fixed share ε of the step's time. A batch runs on the smallest graph that holds it, and padded rows are not free, so the spacing between sizes follows how fast step time grows with batch size, regime by regime. **(a) Decode step rule.** - Padding a batch of `n` by δ costs about `e(n) · δ / n` of its step time, where `e(n) = n · c′(n) / T(n)`. - Bounding the mean cost by ε gives the local step `Δ(n) = 2εn / e(n)`. - One envelope over all measured models, `e ≈ n^(1/3) / 5`, gives `Δ(n) = 10 ε n^(2/3)`. Rounded down to a power of two, with ε = 0.065, that is the decode rule: 64 sizes at 1024. **(b) PIECEWISE rule.** PIECEWISE step time is flat below 1–4K tokens and linear above. The same rule with `e_PW(t) = min(1, t / 4096)` and ε = 0.035 gives the prefill grid: 39 sizes at 8192, which sum to 127,487 tokens (main: 35,335). detail.body:
## 1. Why this change A CUDA graph's batch size means different things for two kinds of step: - A prefill or mixed batch is sized by its **tokens**. - A uniform decode batch, where every request has the same query length `q = 1 + K`, is sized by its **requests** and `q`. On main, model runner V2 captures both from one token list (`cudagraph_capture_sizes`, capped at 1024 tokens on GB200). A decode graph must be a list entry divisible by `q`, so the larger K is, the fewer decode requests the graphs cover, and every mixed batch above 1024 tokens runs eagerly. Example: with the 1024-token cap and K = 7 (`q = 8`), decode graphs cover at most 128 requests. Uniform decode batches above 128 requests exceed main's FULL coverage. This is the "separate prefill/decode graph sizes" item of the Q4 roadmap (#61024). ## 2. What this PR changes This PR adds five configuration fields: a cap and a capture-size list for each kind of graph, plus a token budget for uniform decode graphs. Prefill coverage is configured in tokens; uniform decode coverage is configured in requests. | field | unit | controls | default on SM100 (GB200, B200) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens` | tokens | Maximum token count for prefill, mixed, and fallback decode PIECEWISE graphs | `min(8192, max_num_batched_tokens)` | | `prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes` | tokens | Token counts at which those graphs are captured | Default prefill grid up to the cap: 54 sizes at 8192 tokens | | `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests` | requests | Request-count cap for uniform decode FULL graphs, before applying the token budget | `max_num_seqs` | | `decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes` | requests | Request-count capture sizes, converted by each runner into `n × q` tokens | Default decode grid up to the cap: 64 sizes at 1024 requests, before applying the token budget | | `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens` | tokens | Maximum token count of each uniform decode graph | 8192 | For either kind, setting only a cap generates the default grid up to that cap. An explicit list selects the capture sizes; if a cap is also supplied, the list must fit within it. An empty list disables that kind. The decode request grid is the starting point for capture planning. Each runner uses its own query length `q` and captures only shapes that fit its execution limits and token budget. At the default 1024-request cap, the target captures 64 decode sizes through 1024 requests for K ≤ 7, or 48 sizes through 512 requests for K = 15. Wider target decode batches try the prefill token graphs before falling back to eager execution. The token budget also bounds adaptive-verification graphs. It does not bound one-token draft decodes, which reach `max_num_seqs` whatever the decode caps are (only `[]` turns them off). On other GPUs, the prefill and target decode defaults stay as on main. **How the defaults were chosen.** Defaults trade padding and coverage against memory/startup cost; current padding measurements are in appendix A. The decode budget limits wide graphs (why 8192: section 5.1); explicit lists/caps support workload- and parallelism-specific tuning. The default configuration and tuned performance ceiling are separate evaluation targets.
Grids, other GPUs and edge rules Defaults on other GPUs: the prefill cap is the platform's `max_cudagraph_capture_size` (512 on H100 / H200) and the prefill sizes are main's list; the decode cap is main's reach, 512 / (1 + K) requests, with main's request counts; there is no decode token budget. | what you set for a kind | graphs captured for that kind | | --- | --- | | nothing | the default grid up to the default cap | | a cap only | the default grid up to that cap | | a list only | exactly those sizes | | both | the list; a size above the cap is an error | | `[]` | none | - **Grids.** - **Prefill** / mixed (tokens): 1, 2, 4, every 8 up to 64, four sizes per doubling up to 1024 (…, 512, 640, 768, 896, 1024), then multiples of 256 through 7680, followed by 8192 — **54 capture sizes** at the default cap. Between 64 and 1024 tokens, a mixed batch pads by at most 25%, reducing padding-induced crossings of a model's own shape threshold (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's decoder-replay trim at 768 tokens; DEP section). - **Decode (requests):** every count from 1–6; then 8–16 in steps of 2, 20–48 in steps of 4, 56–128 in steps of 8, 144–352 in steps of 16, and 384–1024 in steps of 32. **64 capture sizes before applying the decode-token budget**; the default 8192-token budget keeps all of them for K ≤ 7 and limits target K=15 to **512 requests / 48 sizes**. - **Adaptive verification (tokens):** 1, 2, 4, 8; then four additional sizes per doubling through 1024—for example, 10, 12, 14, 16, followed by 20, 24, 28, 32. Above 1024, use steps of 128 through 4096, then steps of 256. The cap is `min(decode request cap × (K + 1), max_num_batched_tokens, max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens)`; **K=5 with a 1024-request cap gives 64 sizes through 6144 tokens**. Adaptive verification picks its verify width from the captured sizes, so this grid is finer than the prefill grid. - Sizes above `max_num_batched_tokens` (prefill) or `max_num_seqs` (decode) are dropped with a warning. `[]` for both kinds turns decoder CUDA graphs off. Under `cudagraph_mode` FULL or PIECEWISE (no separate decode routine) every batch uses the prefill sizes; under FULL_DECODE_ONLY the prefill sizes are not captured and do not count toward the recorded maximum. - Setting one kind leaves the other kind's graphs unchanged. Exception: DSpark, DFlash, DFlash2 and LiLiCorr are also capped by the resolved `max_cudagraph_capture_size` divided by their `q`. That value is the largest token count over the language-model/drafter graphs: prefill sizes, target decode `n · q`, one-token draft decodes and adaptive-verification sizes. At the SM100 defaults with K ≤ 7 it is the 8192-token prefill cap. Off SM100 with an EAGLE-family drafter it is the one-token draft decode reach (`max_num_seqs`, 1024), above the 512-token prefill cap. - `cudagraph_capture_sizes` and `max_cudagraph_capture_size` are deprecated on model runner V2. Set alone, they seed both kinds as on main, with a warning; combined with the new fields, they raise. Adaptive verification, DSpark and one-token draft decodes do not reproduce main's graphs under them. Model runner V1 is unchanged and rejects the new fields. ```bash # Before: one cap for both kinds, in tokens. --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 1024}' # After: delete it to take the defaults, or set each kind in its own unit. --compilation-config '{"max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens": 8192, "max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests": 256}' # Prefill instance of a disaggregated deployment: no decode graphs. Adaptive verification # needs decode graphs and is rejected with this; a prefill instance never verifies, so disable it there. --compilation-config '{"decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes": []}' # Decode instance of a disaggregated deployment: FULL decode (and adaptive verification) only, no PIECEWISE graphs. --compilation-config '{"prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes": []}' ```
## 3. Which graphs run ```mermaid flowchart TD C["Resolved config
prefill grid (tokens) · decode grid (requests) · decode budget (tokens)"] C --> T["Target
PIECEWISE: prefill / mixed, by tokens
FULL uniform decode: q = 1 + K, by requests, up to the decode budget
wider decodes: PIECEWISE, or eager without a prefill grid"] T -->|"adaptive verification on"| V["FULL varlen decode, by tokens
replaces the target's uniform decode graphs"] C --> E["EAGLE / EAGLE3 / single-module MTP"] E --> E0["Draft step 0: copies of the target's shapes
PIECEWISE + FULL at q = 1 + K"] E --> E1["Draft steps 1 … K − 1: FULL, q = 1
default request grid through max_num_seqs"] C --> B["DSpark (q = K) · DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr (q = K + 1)
FULL, one graph per draft round"] C --> M["Multi-module MTP (q = 1 + K, the target's layout)
after a decode step: 1 FULL graph with all K modules, by requests
after a prefill / mixed step: K PIECEWISE runs, by tokens"] ``` Each runner owns its graphs and picks among them by its own inputs. A decode step wider than the decode budget falls back to the PIECEWISE prefill graphs; on an instance with an empty prefill grid, such as a disaggregated decode instance, it runs eagerly. The list/cap labels above refer to the exact fields in section 2; a graph mode or attention backend can restrict which paths are available. **YOCO decoder replay: rule unchanged.** Its breakable PIECEWISE grid is still derived from `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, which now follows the prefill cap: 32 sizes up to 8192 tokens (main: 8 up to 1024; memory in section 5). Replays above the grid run eagerly. Forcing every replay eager (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DSpark K5 + AV, GSM8K twice per launch) kept GSM8K answer agreement with the graph runs at the graph-vs-graph level (TP4 / 256K 98.6–99.1% vs 99.0%, DEP4 / 64K 99.0–99.4% vs 99.2%); the debug switch had no counter, so it does not prove that every replay ran eagerly. [Implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cff6224872ad24b10c224bc4186778dcd90a1b21/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py#L26). **DEP applies these grids to per-rank execution batches.** Ranks synchronize execution mode and padding before the final dispatch; API concurrency is not a per-rank capture size. Dynamic SD is currently disabled for DP > 1; AV is a separate setting. [DP dispatch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cff6224872ad24b10c224bc4186778dcd90a1b21/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/dp_utils.py#L43). Every step picks the smallest captured graph that holds it; a step no graph holds runs eagerly. | step | graph | sizes from | decode budget | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | target prefill / mixed batch | PIECEWISE, by tokens | prefill grid | – | | target uniform decode | FULL at `q = 1 + K`, by requests | decode grid; wider decodes run PIECEWISE (eagerly with an empty prefill grid) | yes, up to budget / `q` requests | | target verification with adaptive verification (DSpark, DFlash) | FULL varlen: query lengths 1 … 1 + K in one batch, by tokens | adaptive-verification token grid | yes, up to the budget in tokens | | EAGLE, EAGLE3, single-module MTP: draft step 0 | the target's shape: a PIECEWISE copy for a mixed batch, a FULL copy at the target's `q = 1 + K` for a uniform decode (under dynamic SD, one `q = 1 + k` per tier) | the target's prefill and decode grids | yes, for the FULL copies | | same drafters, draft steps 1 … K − 1 | FULL at `q = 1`, by requests | default request grid through `max_num_seqs`; an empty decode list disables this path | no | | DSpark (`q = K`); DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr (`q = K + 1`) | FULL, one graph per draft round | decode grid, also capped at `max_cudagraph_capture_size` / `q` | yes, up to budget / `q` (all 1024 requests for DSpark K = 7) | | multi-module MTP: draft round after a uniform-decode target step | **one** FULL graph at the target's `q = 1 + K` holding all K module forwards and samplings | the target's decode grid (Inkling K=8: 61 graphs up to 910 requests; main 76 up to 112); wider decodes run as in the next row | yes | | multi-module MTP: draft round after a prefill / mixed target step | **K** breakable PIECEWISE runs, one per module (breakable models, e.g. Inkling, Step5, Kimi-K3); other models run the K modules eagerly | prefill grid (Inkling: 54 sizes up to 8192; main 91 up to 1024) | – | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash YOCO decoder replay | breakable PIECEWISE, by replay tokens (unchanged) | rule unchanged; bound now 8192 (32 sizes; main 8 up to 1024) | no | | n-gram, draft model | none (eager) | – | – | **The rule for `q`:** a FULL decode graph is captured at the query length its runner sees per request. The target and EAGLE-family draft step 0 see the 1 + K verified positions (`q = 1 + K`); later EAGLE-family steps add one token (`q = 1`); DSpark drafts K positions per round (`q = K`); DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr and multi-module MTP draft K + 1 (`q = K + 1`). Dynamic SD changes the target's verification length. EAGLE-family drafters also shorten their drafting sequence, while DSpark and DFlash currently retain their maximum draft-block width (K = 7: all 1024 requests under the 8192-token budget). A graph for `n` requests holds `n · q` tokens, which is what the decode budget bounds. **The decode budget** applies to every FULL uniform-decode graph with `q > 1`: the target's, the drafter copies of it, DSpark, DFlash and multi-module MTP. Each runner divides it by its own `q`: at K ≤ 7 the target and every drafter reach the 1024-request cap, while at K = 11 the target (`q = 12`) reaches 682 requests and DSpark (`q = 11`) 744. Why 8192: section 5.1. Adaptive verification's token-keyed graphs stop at the budget too. One-token draft decodes (`q = 1`, at most `max_num_seqs` tokens) are not bounded by it. **Graph count, one example:** MiniMax-M3 with EAGLE3 K = 3 at the GB200 defaults. | runner | this PR | main | | --- | --- | --- | | target PIECEWISE | 54, up to 8192 tokens | 83, up to 1024 tokens | | target FULL (`q = 4`) | 64, up to 1024 requests | 81, up to 256 requests | | drafter step 0 (copies of the target's) | 54 + 64 | 83 + 81 | | drafter steps 1–2 (`q = 1`) | 64, up to 1024 requests | 83, up to 1024 requests | | **total** | **300** | **411** | Current total memory is in section 5. Counts for every runner, K, dynamic SD tier and for GPUs other than SM100: appendix G (recomputed on the measured base; every launch's logged capture counts match).
Scope: vision encoder and TPU graph planning The new prefill/decode fields configure **GPU language-model and drafter graphs**. Vision-encoder graphs have an independent shape contract; TPU uses XLA compilation rather than CUDA graph replay. | Component | Size / execution contract | Controls | | --- | --- | --- | | GPU vision encoder | Visual **output tokens**, item/frame capacity, model paths and optional shape axes; captures a whole encoder path, including attention, with eager fallback | `cudagraph_mm_encoder`, `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch` | | GPU language-model prefill / decode | Scheduled tokens / requests × query length; PIECEWISE / FULL as described above | This PR's prefill/decode fields | | TPU language-model backbone | Token and request buckets select JAX/XLA executable shapes; these are not CUDA FULL/PW graphs | `MIN_TOKEN_BUCKET`, `VLLM_TPU_BUCKET_PADDING_GAP`, `additional_config.compilation_sizes`, `ATTN_BUCKETIZED_NUM_REQS` / `ATTN_CUSTOM_NUM_REQS_BUCKETS` | | TPU vision encoder, supported budget-manager path | Reuses GPU encoder budget generation and packing, with JIT compilation replacing CUDA capture/replay | Existing `cudagraph_mm_encoder` / `encoder_cudagraph_*` fields | **Vision defaults and counts.** Encoder capture is off by default. Its empty budget list means **automatic sizing**, unlike the new decoder lists where `[]` disables that kind. Budgets double from a model-provided minimum and include the maximum. For Qwen3-VL, with `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` and sufficient context, this gives `[64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192]`: **8 graphs**. Model paths and extra axes multiply the count: at the same cap, Gemma4 with five enabled row widths has **40**, and DeepSeek-OCR's global/local paths have **14**. These are source-derived examples, not measured captures in this PR. Multi-path models may regenerate their own per-path grids from the maximum; an explicit encoder list is not universally an exact per-path list. [Planner and count formula](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/vllm/v1/worker/encoder_cudagraph.py#L82-L280). Changing the decoder prefill cap alone does not resize encoder graphs. Encoder auto-sizing can depend on the scheduler token cap and model context. Encoder preparation and cached-output cloning remain outside graph replay. `compile_mm_encoder` is a separate compilation switch; `enforce_eager` disables encoder capture, whereas decoder mode `NONE` alone does not. **Memory / performance.** Encoder capture owns a separate shared graph pool plus persistent per-budget input/output buffers; runtime embedding caches and gather buffers add further costs. Graph count alone does not determine GiB. Upstream's GB200 Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B benchmark reports mean encoder latency **5.42 → 4.36 ms** with FLASHINFER and an explicit nine-size grid; that is an encoder benchmark, not an E2E result from this PR. See the [design and reproduction commands](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md). No encoder-specific memory measurement is claimed here. The pinned base already checks `runner.needs_cudagraph_capture()` before returning early for decoder mode `NONE`; the earlier encoder-only profiling caveat is resolved in the base ([current guard](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/08e3f264583e57199c167c577f3b445a58c155ab/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L944-L948)). Encoder-specific memory and runtime evaluation remain outside this refresh. **TPU scope.** At plugin `7840339bd3`, a DP1 configuration with an 8192-token cap and default minimum 16 has **10 token buckets**, doubling from 16 to 8192. This is not the total executable count: request buckets, embedding/PCP variants, SD and helper functions add variants. A positive padding-gap setting trades more compiled shapes for less padding. This PR's split CUDA-grid fields do not configure those TPU backbone buckets. The TPU vision manager already shares the encoder planner, but currently declines extra capture axes and assumes a single default path. [Token buckets](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/utils.py#L163-L263), [runner](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/tpu_runner.py#L1099-L1207), [vision JIT manager](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/mm_encoder_jit_manager.py). No TPU runtime or HBM validation is claimed. **Integration direction:** share shape planning, dispatch diagnostics and memory accounting while retaining explicit units and backend execution. A concrete planning follow-up is to prune infeasible budget/axis pairs: in the Gemma4 example above, 10 of 40 pairs have a budget below one image/frame row width and cannot be selected for nonempty replay. This is a source-derived pruning opportunity, not a measured memory saving ([shape contract](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py#L1710-L1900)). Keep encoder budget overrides; do not silently copy the decoder grid into vision or TPU. Per-path/axis budgets remain follow-ups; encoder-only profiling is already handled by the pinned base. This refresh does not add encoder changes.
## 4. Measured results Head `c85b0733bf`, on main `6dc6d2c0f3`. Section 5 and the newest rows below were measured on main `254a2a3390`, which includes the indexer chunking (#64806) and #65041. Throughput and correctness below were measured on main `51c6dfd8c8`, which includes the extensible KV cache (#56492), with the earlier 4096-token decode budget; the 8192 default changes only uniform decode steps wider than 4096 tokens, measured in section 5.1. Memory against current main is in section 5. The measured CG stack is this PR plus **2 GiB indexer chunking (#64806)**; rows marked † also carry the masked-candidate-consumer chunking, now in #64806, and the empty-prefill-chunk fix, now on main (#65046). Merged persistent BF16 top-k (#64138), recursive aux-output weakrefs (#63427), AV profiling-cache cleanup, and YOCO/target capture-stream sharing (#63155) are already in the base. No other optimizations are added. Every comparison is **pure main against CG+chunk**, with the default memory utilization 1.0. Both arms use the same model weights within each comparison. These measure deployment defaults at fixed SD settings, not a tuned performance frontier. Both arms use the same prebuilt native libraries; Python source revisions are the pins above. Appendix I gives the commands to reproduce these measurements. ### 4.1 Correctness GSM8K has 1319 questions. ### 5.2 DFlash graph memory and the MiMo limitation DFlash and DFlash2 drafters have no PIECEWISE fallback, so at K7–K8 the 8192-token budget gives their FULL graphs up to 8190 tokens (main: about 1024). On MiMo this adds 10.2 GiB of graph memory, from two sources. The target's widest prefill graph (8192 tokens) takes 5.4 GiB more than main's (1024 tokens), mostly FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE workspace. The DFlash drafter's widest graph (8190 tokens) takes 5.45 GiB, against 0.68 GiB on main, because it materializes full-vocabulary draft logits three times (the TP all-gather output, a contiguous copy and the vocabulary remap; about 2.07 GiB each). None of this is a leak. `graph_capture()` gives the target and the drafter separate capture streams, and the caching allocator keeps free graph-pool blocks per stream, so neither runner reuses the other's free blocks. Appendix A. How the grids were chosen **Data.** The rule was derived from traces on earlier PR heads; the padding cost in (c) is a current measurement. **The rule.** Each grid captures a graph wherever padding to the next size would cost more than a fixed share ε of the step's time. A batch runs on the smallest graph that holds it, and padded rows are not free, so the spacing between sizes follows how fast step time grows with batch size, regime by regime. **(a) Decode step rule.** - Padding a batch of `n` by δ costs about `e(n) · δ / n` of its step time, where `e(n) = n · c′(n) / T(n)`. - Bounding the mean cost by ε gives the local step `Δ(n) = 2εn / e(n)`. - One envelope over all measured models, `e ≈ n^(1/3) / 5`, gives `Δ(n) = 10 ε n^(2/3)`. Rounded down to a power of two, with ε = 0.065, that is the decode rule: 64 sizes at 1024. **(b) PIECEWISE rule.** PIECEWISE step time is flat below 1–4K tokens and linear above. The same rule with `e_PW(t) = min(1, t / 4096)` and ε = 0.035 gives the prefill grid: 39 sizes at 8192, which sum to 127,487 tokens (main: 35,335). The default now also caps the step at a quarter of the size below 1024 (at least 8), giving 54 sizes; it bounds small-size padding at 25% so a padded size cannot jump across a model's own threshold (DEP section). **(c) Current padding cost.** Single prefill (pure) or one prefill injected into 16 running decodes (mixed), no SD, no prefix cache, 8192 batched tokens; median of 15 per point, with the dispatch checked for each point. Appendix F. Dense models on one GPU: why the gain is small Measured on Qwen3.8-27B with MTP K=3 on one GB200 (ShareGPT, 1024 output tokens): - **Throughput equals main's** within launch noise (0.99× / 0.99× / 1.00× at C1 / C16 / C256). - **KV cache is 1.8% smaller**, because the wider graphs take memory on a GPU that has little to spare (CUDA graph 2.49 → 4.62 GiB). At 256 concurrent requests, requests queue in waves, so the TTFT median (9.2 → 14.7 s) falls between the waves while the mean (+2%) and throughput barely change. **Why.** A dense model on one GPU is GPU-bound from about 1.5K tokens per step: a PIECEWISE graph shortens a mixed step, but the next step grows by the same amount, so the pair takes the same time. The host launch time that the graph removes was already hidden behind GPU work. Large MoE models with tensor or expert parallelism are the opposite: many small kernels per layer make the host the bottleneck, which is where this PR's gains come from. **For users.** On such models, wide graphs buy little throughput and cost KV cache. Where KV capacity matters more, lowering `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens` and `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens` trades the unused graph width back for KV cache; the right values depend on the model and workload. A per-model default is follow-up 10.

 Then it will only capture cudagraph for the specified sizes. It can be useful to have fine-grained control over the cudagraph capture.
 
+With model runner V2, `cudagraph_capture_sizes` and `max_cudagraph_capture_size` are deprecated. Two independent pairs set the graphs instead, and setting one never changes the other:
+
+- `prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes` and `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens`, in **tokens**: graphs for batches with a prefill, and for any batch whose requests have different query lengths.
+- `decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes` and `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests`, in **requests**: FULL graphs for uniform decode batches, whose requests all have the same query length `q` (1 + `num_speculative_tokens` for the target model; K or K + 1 for DSpark, DFlash and multi-module MTP drafters). A graph of `n` requests holds `n * q` tokens.
+
+`max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens` (default 8192 on SM100, the default prefill ceiling; no budget elsewhere) also bounds each uniform decode graph at `n * q` tokens, so a large `num_speculative_tokens` does not spend KV cache memory on very wide decode graphs. Wider decode batches take the prefill graphs.
+
+One-token draft decodes (the EAGLE, EAGLE3 and MTP draft steps after the first) take the default request-count grid up to `max_num_seqs`, whatever the decode request sizes are (`[]` still turns them off): their graphs are small, and an eager draft step costs its host launch time.
+
+With adaptive verification, the target model's decode batches mix query lengths, so they take token-keyed graphs. Those graphs reach `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens, within `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens`; the decode request sizes then set only the draft decode graphs.
+
+Set either a list or a cap; a cap captures the default grid of sizes up to it. Larger caps and longer lists capture more and wider graphs, which take memory from the KV cache and lengthen startup. Decode graphs no wider than the widest prefill graph mostly reuse its memory in the shared graph pool. For example, a prefill instance of a disaggregated deployment can skip decode graphs:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B \
+  --compilation-config '{"decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes": []}'
+```
+
 ### Full Cudagraph capture
 
 It is possible to include attention as part of the cudagraph if using an attention backend that is cudagraph compatible. This can improve performance in some cases such as decode speed for smaller models or MOEs. See [CUDA Graphs](cuda_graphs.md) for more details.

@yewentao256 Thanks! In response to [your review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63406#pullrequestreview-5674091216), here are the initial findings:

- **Padding can cause regressions**, particularly on the dense Qwen3.8-27B model: mixed-batch latency increased by up to 12% at the tested sizes with the previous grid.
- **The large MoE models generally benefited**, especially above main's 1024-token capture cap. MiniMax showed smaller 4–7% increases at some sub-1K points, with launch-to-launch variation; those need confirmation.
- **The updated grid reduces padding in this intermediate range.** 384, 640 and 896 tokens now match exact capture sizes; 769 rounds up to 896 instead of 1024.

**Initial mixed-batch latency: PR grid / main's grid** (lower is better). Both configurations ran on the same PR build, `cff6224872`, changing only the prefill capture sizes. These results use the **previous 39-size grid**, not the current 54-size default.

GB200, no SD or prefix caching; 16 decoding requests plus one injected prefill request, totaling the actual token count above. Main's size list falls back to eager above 1024 tokens, so the larger-size comparisons include the benefit of wider graph coverage.

Some H200 (SM90) data on prefill padding that may help with the regression question above. This PR keeps the 512-token ceiling off SM100, so all of this is about Hopper.
